cust_julia: Hey team — after we pinned embed-large-v2 for stability some of our embedding calls started returning vectors of length 256 instead of 512. Indexing pipeline throws. Happens roughly 1 in 10 requests, random across batches. Request ids: r_20240301_98123, r_20240301_98156. Any idea?
kevin_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal request (headers + body) you used for the failing call and confirm the exact model string you pinned?
cust_julia: Sure. We pinned using our UI to: `embed-large-v2@2024-03-01-lock`. Here's the curl we use (multi-input batching):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Model-Pin: embed-large-v2@2024-03-01-lock" \
  -d '{"inputs": ["doc A","doc B","doc C","doc D"], "max_tokens": 0}'
```
Response for r_20240301_98123 had first two items 512 floats, last two items 256 floats.
kevin_support: Thanks — escalating to runtime. @maya_runtime can you take traces for those request ids and check if any fallback/variant substitution happened?
maya_runtime: Looking now. I pulled the trace for r_20240301_98123 — I see a mixed execution path: two shards executed on `embed-large-v2.q8` (512-d) and two on `embed-small-256.q8` (256-d). There's a routing decision logged: `route: pinned_variant_unavailable -> fallback: compatible_variant` with batchpad filling.
cust_julia: We didn't expect fallbacks — we pinned to keep outputs stable. Is fallback allowed for pinned variants?
ajay_eng_oncall: Pinning is supposed to prevent automatic fallback to a different variant. The logs show a LRU pool eviction on one node right before the request and the scheduler incorrectly considered the pinned variant unavailable and selected a compatibility fallback. That should be blocked by pin flag.
sophie_sre: Deploy-bot shows a scheduled kernel update at 02:15 UTC on 2024-03-01 to a subset of gpu-nodes (canary). Node gn-12 reported `out-of-memory evict` then rejoined, which likely triggered transient capacity signals.
kevin_support: OK — short-term mitigation options: 1) unpin to allow safe fallback, 2) force route to hosted `embed-large-v2` (non-pinned) for that org, or 3) rollback the canary patch on the affected pool. Which do you prefer?
cust_julia: We need deterministic embedding size for indexing so unpin isn't acceptable. Rolling back canary if that's the root cause would be fine.
ajay_eng_oncall: We'll rollback the node patch on the affected pool and add a guard to ensure pinned variants are not eligible for compatibility fallback. I'll open a hotfix.
maya_runtime: For reproducibility: tried a local stress test with batch sizes 1..8 and injecting a transient node unavailability; reproduced mixed-dim outputs when pin flag was present + scheduler hit an edge-case where partial batch affinity allowed cross-variant placement. Repro steps:
```
# reproduce (internal)
python tests/repro/embed_pin_batchpad_repro.py \
  --model embed-large-v2@2024-03-01-lock \
  --batch-size 4 --inject-node-drop gn-12 --repeat 100
```
Result: ~8% of runs triggered mixed vector widths.
kevin_support: Patch plan: 1) rollback canary on pool `gpu-canary-eu-1`, 2) apply guard in scheduler to honor pin header before fallback selection, 3) run targeted canary with additional checks. ETA for rollback: 20m, hotfix for scheduler: ~3h.
sophie_sre: Rollback started — deploy-bot: `rollback gpu-canary-eu-1 -> revision 2024-02-28` (in progress).
cust_julia: Noted. Please keep us updated, we have a batch index job scheduled in ~1.5h and would like it to succeed.
sophie_sre: Rollback complete. Health checks green across the pool.
maya_runtime: Re-ran a throttled repro against live with injected node behavior — no more mixed-dim responses across 500 runs.
ajay_eng_oncall: Hotfix merged to main to prevent fallback when X-Model-Pin header present. We'll promote to canary in 1h with stricter assertions.
cust_julia: Thanks team — can you confirm we should re-pin after higher-level rollout or leave as-is?
ajay_eng_oncall: You can keep the pin. The hotfix ensures pin is respected. We'll notify once the canary passes.
kevin_support: I'll follow up with a ticket and include the request ids + cluster logs. Apologies for the disruption, and thanks for the quick repro steps, Julia. :pray:
cust_julia: Appreciate it — thanks!
